entities.summary:
The Battle of Bunker Hill was a pivotal event in the American Revolutionary War, fought on June 17, 1775, in Charlestown, Massachusetts. 

This battle was a defining moment in the war, as it was the first major battle between the British and the colonists. The British forces, led by General William Howe and General Henry Clinton, attacked the colonial forces, who were led by Colonel Joseph Warren and Colonel William Prescott. The battle was fierce and bloody, with both sides suffering heavy casualties. 

The battle had a significant impact on the war, as it gave the colonists a much-needed victory and boosted their morale. The British, on the other hand, suffered heavy losses and were forced to retreat. The battle also marked a turning point in the war, as it showed that the colonists were capable of resisting the British army. 

The battle of Bunker Hill has become a legendary event in American history, symbolizing the bravery and determination of the colonists in their fight for independence. As the famous American general, Nathanael Greene, said: 'I wish I could have seen the battle of Bunker Hill, it would have been a charming sight to behold.'
